findings.heading: "Wide" format / "Geniş" format
findings.proposition: English: the column headers represent VALUES of a hypothetical "age group" variable. Turkish: the column headers represent the hypothetical "age group" VARIABLE itself ("bunlar hipotetik bir 'yaş grubu' *değişkenini* temsil eder").
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish sentence contradicts itself: it first says the headers do not represent variables, then says they represent a variable. The reader loses the central tidy-data argument for why this table must be pivoted, and may conclude the wide layout is already tidy.

findings.heading: "Wide" format / "Geniş" format
findings.proposition: English: the DATES of the observations range from count_data$data_date min() to max(). Turkish: "bu sayı" (this number/count) varies between count_data$data_date min() and max(), attaching the range to the malaria counts rather than to the dates.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader takes the min/max of the date column as the range of the case counts, and so misreads what the 3,038 rows span. They lose the fact that the dataset covers a fixed date window across the 65 facilities.

findings.heading: Pivot wider / Daha geniş olarak pivotlama
findings.proposition: The Turkish prose names the argument `name_from`; the chunk beside it (pivoting.tr.qmd:394-401) uses `names_from = gender`. There is no `name_from` argument in pivot_wider().
findings.reader_consequence: A reader who types `name_from` gets an error, or silently passes an unmatched argument, and cannot reproduce table_wide.

findings.heading: Pivoting data of multiple classes / Birden çok sınıfa ait verinin pivotlanması
findings.proposition: The Turkish prose names the argument `name_sep`; the chunk beside it (pivoting.tr.qmd:295-307) uses `names_sep = "_"`. There is no `name_sep` argument in pivot_longer().
findings.reader_consequence: A reader following the two-bullet instruction writes `name_sep = "_"`, the split on the underscore never happens, and the ".value" mechanism the whole section teaches fails.

findings.heading: Standard pivoting
findings.proposition: The Turkish prose names the tidyselect helper `start_with()`; the chunk beside it (pivoting.tr.qmd:164-170) uses `starts_with("malaria_")`. There is no `start_with()` function in tidyselect.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader who copies `start_with("malaria_")` from the prose gets "could not find function" and cannot select the four malaria columns by prefix.

findings.heading: Pivot wider / Daha geniş olarak pivotlama
findings.proposition: English states that the columns given to `id_cols = ` "will thus identify each row". The Turkish sentence ends without this purpose clause, and instead garbles it into "döndürülmemesi gereken satırları içeren sütun adları vektörü" (a vector of column names containing the rows that should not be pivoted).
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish reader is not told what id_cols is FOR, namely that the named columns become the row identifiers of the wide table. They cannot decide which columns to pass, which is exactly the choice the N.B. at the end of the Fill section asks them to make.

findings.heading: Standard pivoting
findings.proposition: English says mapping age_group to `fill = ` produces a STACKED bar chart ("a stacked bar chart, by age group"). The Turkish says only "çubuk grafikte" (in a bar chart), dropping "stacked".
findings.reader_consequence: The reader is not told that the bars stack, so the double-height artefact discussed two segments later (malaria_tot added on top of the three age groups) is harder to connect to the mapping just made.
